top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer proposed, and on the common criteria he is a defensible laureate. As publicly described, Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid show a distinctive voice. They join bodily and mnemonic material to large recursive structures in long, syntactically ambitious prose, which is a formal and imaginative achievement. The project reads as cumulative, running from the lyric work through the large novels, and the attribution is clean: one writer, one language. The citation is narrowed so that the prose carries the claim and poetry is named only as its lyric root. It makes no claim about a lifetime's work, completeness or lineage. Unresolved uncertainties remain. Sentence-level achievement in Romanian can be judged only through translation and critical report, a limit that applies equally to any language-bound candidate. Coverage of the poetry and essays in translation is thinner. It is not established which volumes beyond Blinding and Solenoid show sustained quality, or whether the inward, maximalist mode amounts to breadth of significance. I have not independently verified any text. These doubts do not outweigh the case for the award, so I rank P001 above no award (P000).
